power.capacity-scope: the load the PDU can hand on, 3.7 kW (the "Output kW" column of the maker's table). It is not what the PDU draws itself

occupant-attrs.data-description: ETH2 and ETH1, the two redundant network jacks
ETH2 and ETH1, the two redundant network jacks
the CAN bus jack for CMC III sensors
the USB port for firmware updates and data logging

configs.description: The PDU as it ships: the fixed cord and the two push-button attachments on it. The connector lock for IEC C14 and C20 connectors, the universal mounting kit and the mounting adaptor are not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the two sources disagree. The data sheet says black anodised RAL 9005 ("other colours may be configured"), drawn as #0e0e10. The photographs of the metered family show a natural silver-grey extrusion, median #8a8a8a over 383777 pixels of photograph 78_2802, and dark graphite plates. Black is drawn, as the data sheet states. Nine of the ten basic Rittal devices on main draw silver, #b9bbbe.
gaps.wanted: a rating plate or order note naming the finish of this SKU.

gaps.note: photograph 78_3236 shows a small module with two sockets, two arrows and dots at the foot end of one phase of a three-phase strip. No held document says which listed SKU carries it, so it is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a document that names the SKU and draws the module.

gaps.note: fig. 21 item 12 calls the jack a "CAN bus connection (daisy chain) for CMC III sensors, 24 V, 1 A". The instructions state no bit rate for it. It carries no speed and the search is recorded here.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the CAN bus bit rate.

gaps.note: no photograph of this SKU shows what is printed beside the outlets. The placement ids stand.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the printed outlet numbers.

gaps.note: the three outlet cells are drawn in the dark cell colour, as no held picture of a single-phase unit shows a coloured plate. The edges of each cell are read from the drawing.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front with a scale.

gaps.note: the mounting adaptor 7000.688 and the universal mounting kit are named and not drawn.

gaps.wanted: one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `power` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

button-plates.note: The plan view of page 3 draws each button plate 25.0 along the strip and 35.0 across. Two lines stand 5.0 mm in from its ends and three rings, 15.0, 7.5 and 3.7 across, sit at its centre. They are the part rittal/pdu-metered-button@1, read from the vector paths. Two lines of 24.0 mm cross at its centre, one across the strip and one along it, under the rings. The label cover carries its double rim, read the same way.

c13-frames.note: Each C13 of the front view of page 3 sits in a rounded outer frame, 28.0 along the strip and 35.8 across, with R2.5 corners. It is drawn here as decor. Neighbouring frames stand 28.35 apart and nearly touch. The frames were read from the page's vector paths, twice, and from a 1200 dpi crop. The part std/c13-outlet@1 draws the well, nose and contacts inside each frame. The outlets stand up to 0.52 mm from their frame centre and are not moved. Pages 3 and 18 give the well chamfers of 6.5 mm and the nose 5.0 mm, read twice at the upper and lower corner. The shared part draws 5.4 and 4.5, so its diagonals stand 0.78 and 0.37 mm from the drawing's. The well's corner stands 3.1 mm from the frame's end and 2.9 mm from its side. Decor has no chamfer or polyline shape (device.schema.json line 1496 lists `rect`, `d-sub` and `slot`) and the part is shared, so they are not changed.

c19-frames.note: The C19 of the front view of page 3 sits in two rounded frames. The outer one is 42.1 along the strip and 34.11 across, with R1.5 corners, and is drawn here. The inner one is 34.7 by 26.7 with R4.5 corners, 3.65 mm inside it. It is the mouth that std/c19-outlet@1 draws at 35.6 by 27.7, so it is not drawn twice. The outer frame was read from the page's vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render.

cell-lines.note: The front view of page 3 draws full-height lines across the strip at the ends of each block of outlets. They are drawn as 0.2 mm lines, or 0.35 mm where the drawing doubles a line 0.2 mm apart. They were read from the vector paths. Between two C13 the drawing has no line, only the frames.

chassis.note: drawing - length 845 (the dimension of the front view and the table of page 1). Width is 44 (the data sheet's "44 mm (1 U)"), depth 72.1 (the side view's dimension). The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) prints "PDU enclosure depth 70 mm" and the end view 109. The 109 is the body with the cable gland standing out of the front and the button out of the back. The 70 is the extrusion profile. 72.1 is drawn, as on the basic devices.

colour.note: The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) says "Aluminium, anodised in RAL 9005 (black, other colours may be configured)", so the body is drawn black. The screen value #0e0e10 is the usual one for RAL 9005 and is estimated. The two photographs of the metered family show a natural silver-grey extrusion, median #8a8a8a over 383777 pixels of photograph 78_2802. They also show dark graphite plates, #2b2b2c over 301257 pixels. Colours are a later touch. The gap below names both.

controller.note: drawing - the controller cell is 602.39 to 802.41 of page 3, at the head end. Its parts are the PDU controller plate and two RJ45 jacks (ETH2 and ETH1). The rest are an RJ12 jack (RS232), an RJ45 jack (CAN bus), a USB-A port and two small headers. They are read as the DK 7979.238 page reads them, and the cell lines agree to 0.3 mm. Rittal, "Montage-, Installations- und Betriebsanleitung" for the PDU metered (7979204), fig. 21 names each of them. The data sheet calls the RS232 port RJ12 and the library's `rj11` key is the same six-position body. Each jack is drawn unrotated with its pins up.

dcim.note: the input is one power port from the cord part and each outlet a power outlet it feeds. C13 and C19 export as the IEC types. The CEE plug exports as `other` with a label. The jacks export as ports of their own type.

end-views.note: The end view of page 3 draws the 44.0 by 72.1 mm section of the body, plain. Its outline is drawn on the top and the bottom face. The gland, the cover and the button stand outside the section, 109 mm in all. They are not drawn on the face, for the reason given for the side views. The view does not tell the two ends apart, so both are built from it.

front.note: drawing - the front view of page 3, mm from the foot end. The foot cell is 0 to 72.1 with the gland ring. The cord cell runs to 195.89 with a raised label cover in it. A block of six C13 cells runs to 376.3, a second to 556.97, and a C19 cell to 602.39. The controller runs to 802.41, a blank cell to 826.42, and the head cap to 845. Outlets count from the foot. The C13 long axis is across the strip and the C19 long axis along it.

head-cap-ribs.note: The head cap in the front view of page 3 has one full-width line, 10.1 mm from the head end. It is a pair of lines 0.2 mm apart and is drawn as one 0.35 mm line. It was read from the page's vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render. The photographs are too small to count it.

input.note: datasheet - dri1308088en p.1 gives 230 V, 16 A for this SKU, three wires and a 3 m cable of type H05-VV. A single-phase input states no wiring. The unit has a fixed cord and no inlet. `plug-rating-a` is not written, as the data sheet rates the unit and not the plug. The data sheet gives circuit-breakers only for 32 A versions, so none is drawn.

label-cover.note: The label cover in the cord cell is the part rittal/pdu-cover-plate@1. The front view gives its rectangle. The side view of page 18 draws it as a trapezoid 13.2 mm proud, read at 600 and 1200 dpi. The part builds the sloped ends.

lamps.note: Instructions p.18 to 19, tables 1 to 4. Every lamp is drawn dark and states its colours. POWER is green. The multi-LED STATUS lamp is green, orange or red. It is blue for a changed position and white for a sensor update. Two flashing codes cycle colours in the table. Device-detected cycles green, orange and red. Device-lost alternates red and blue. Each is stated here as one colour, green and red, which is a single-colour approximation of the printed cycle. The CAN jack has a green and a red lamp and each Ethernet jack a green and an orange one. The two CAN lamps are estimated and stand 1.6 mm toward the head, so neither straddles the plate's section line. The drawing shows no lamp there. Fig. 21 shows no lit lamp. Its green #3baa39 over 2251 pixels is the ETH1 jack body. Its yellow #f0f130 over 287 pixels is a contact pad, in a 200 dpi render of page 18. The lit colours here are the library's usual values, estimated.

lifecycle.note: the maker's page lists the SKU among the metered variants. No end-of-life notice was found in the pages read.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S DIMENSIONED DRAWING. Rittal, "Technical details, Power Distribution Unit, Metered version" (dri2108029en, 08.2023), PDF page 3, DK 7979.210. The page also holds the DK 7979.204 above it. The page has a plan view, a side view, an end view and a front view, with the circuit diagram below. The cell lines of the front view were read from a 600 dpi render at the drawing's own scale. The 845 overall length reads 1.937 px per mm. Each cell edge is a full-height line. Good to about 1 mm. Each outlet sits in its cell at the lines the drawing of this page shows inside the cell.

mount.note: `rack-side`, the library's way to say a part stands vertically beside an upright. It hangs on the two push-button attachments of the plan view, dimensioned 622.3 apart. The data sheet's "PDU mounting options" are the enclosure frame at the side of the 482.6 mm mounting frame and the cable route. The mounting adaptor 7000.688 is an accessory and is not drawn. `ru: 19` is the 845 mm it runs, 845 / 44.45 = 19.0.

mounting-buttons.note: drawing - the plan view of page 3 shows two buttons 622.3 apart (dimensioned). Their plates read 98.85 to 123.63 and 720.86 to 745.89 from the foot end, 25.2 long. The foot end of the plan view is taken to be the end of the front view's foot cell.

outlets.note: datasheet and drawing - the table of page 1 ("PDU metered") lists DK 7979.210. It gives 1~, 16 A, 3.7 kW, CEE input, 12 IEC C13 and 1 IEC C19, measuring per phase, 845 mm. std/c13-outlet@1 and std/c19-outlet@1. None is switched and none has a lamp. NO OUTLET NAME IS WRITTEN. No held photograph is of this SKU and the outlets keep their placement ids, counted from the foot.

phase-plates.note: The instructions (7979204) and the data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) mark phases for three-phase PDUs only, pink, black and white. This unit is single-phase and its drawing on page 3 shows no marking. The three outlet cells are drawn in the dark cell colour of the basic family, #1d1d1f. The short strip of photograph 78_3236 shows plain outlets with no coloured plate.

plan-circles.note: The plan view of page 3 shows one small circle on the centre line, at 422.5 mm from the foot, the mid-length. It reads 2.4 mm across, twice at 600 dpi. Nothing says what it is. It is drawn on the back as a dark disc, marked as estimated.

plate-outline.note: The controller plate steps in by 0.6 mm on each side over the last 23.0 mm of each end. An inner rim line runs 1.4 mm inside each end section. Both are read from a 1800 dpi render of page 18. The foot end is drawn by the device and the head end by the controller part.

plate-sections.note: The controller plate in the front view of page 3 has five full-height section lines. They are at 74.0, 104.0, 131.0, 142.7 and 160.0 mm from the head end of the plate. They were read from the vector paths and from a 1800 dpi render. The first is in rittal/pdu-controller@1 and the other four are drawn here.

rear.note: drawing - the plan view of page 3 draws two grooves 3.0 wide and a ridge 1.55 wide with a line along its crest. It also draws two buttons. The grooves and the ridge run 597.3 mm between the plates, from 124.1 to 721.4 from the head end. They also run from each strip end to its plate. The head run starts 3.51 mm from the head end. The foot run stops 3.0 mm short of the foot end. They were read from the vector paths, twice. The mid circle is drawn by `mark-1`.

side-views.note: The side view of page 3 draws the body as a 72.1 by 845 rectangle. Its front edge has a notch, 2.1 mm deep and 0.2 to 0.36 wide, at each cell line. The outline and the notches were read from the vector paths, twice, and are drawn as decor. The gland, the label cover, the outlet bars and the two button feet stand outside that rectangle, past the face. Decor is clipped to the face (L150) and the depth stays 72.1, so they are not drawn on it. The cover and the buttons stand out in 3D as the relief of their parts. The drawing shows one side and the other is built the same, mirrored.

usb-port.note: The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) calls the port "USB 2.0 port (USB-A)", so it is std/usb-a@1 in its white-tongue skin. Fig. 21 item 15 and photograph 78_2802 show a silver-white shell and no trident. The shell reads #c5c5c5 over 309 pixels of a 200 dpi render of page 18. It is drawn as a plate behind the port, as the device's own decor. No shared part draws a USB-A metal shell, and the white-tongue part is reused for the tongue. The shell takes its place and size from the vector paths, 12.5 by 5.11 mm. The part's tongue is 10.2 mm wide against 11.1 drawn, so its centre stands on the drawn centre.
